text:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High p99 latency on streaming inference endpoints (route=/v1/streaming/generate). Paging @Maya. metrics snapshot: p95 1.2s -> 2.8s, p99 4.3s -> 12.7s, error_rate +2.1pp. Some streams are stalling / reconnecting. Trace sample: trace_id=trc_8f3b. Possible dependencies implicated: control-plane config fetch and feature-flag service.

Maya (SRE): taking this incident. First pass triage — opening dashboards, grabbing traces. Noticed a cluster of traces where the inference path blocks waiting on `configfetch` RPCs (~600-900ms) then retries cascade. Also seeing increased 429s from featureflag-service. Will check DB pools + control-plane logs.

Ira (mlops): adding context — we deployed a feature-flag rollout last night that added a synchronous feature flag check on streaming init. Featureflag service started returning 429s around the same time as the spike. Instrumented metric: `featureflags.requests_429_1m` jumped from ~2 -> ~320. We have no local TTL for flags right now (always fetch on start).

Lin (infra): checking control-plane pods (prod). K8s snapshot: control-plane-configfetch-0/1/2 at ~95% CPU in the last 10m. Logs show repeated timeouts to auth-db and transient `pool exhausted` warnings. Snippet from pod logs:

```
2026-03-14T01:46:12Z WARN configfetch Fetch timeout to auth-db (timeout=400ms) trace=trc_8f3b
2026-03-14T01:46:13Z ERROR featureflags 429 returning due to rate limit, key=ff-service
2026-03-14T01:46:14Z WARN configfetch retrying sync for request=rid_9a8
2026-03-14T01:46:15Z ERROR db pool exhausted, waiting (max_open_conns=50)
```

Lin: running quick DB check: `SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state = 'active' AND query LIKE '%SELECT%config%';` shows ~48 active long-running queries.

Sam (eng-runtime): quick mitigation suggestions: 1) bind a short local TTL for feature flags so streaming clients don't block on control-plane fetch; 2) enable circuit-breaker on configfetch RPCs to fail-fast and use last-known-good; 3) increase DB connection pool temporarily on configfetch pods; 4) apply backoff + jitter for FF calls. I can push a patch for env overrides and a hotfix to configfetch to return cached values on error.

Maya (SRE): agreed. Mitigation plan (immediate):
- set FEATUREFLAGS_CACHE_TTL=300 on control-plane sidecars to allow 5m local caching
- add a circuit-breaker env `CONFIGFETCH_CB_MS=200` so requests >200ms short-circuit to cached value
- scale up configfetch deployment to +2 replicas and bump DB pool from 50 -> 80 as emergency measure
- temporarily relax rate-limit on ff-service from 1000r/s -> 2000r/s for 15m to drain backlog (ops approval required)

Ira (mlops): I can prepare a client-side shim to use cached flags for streaming init if server returns 429 or times out. Will send PR for review and a feature gate to enable fast.

Lin (infra): applying the env patch now. Command: `kubectl set env deployment/configfetch FEATUREFLAGS_CACHE_TTL=300 CONFIGFETCH_CB_MS=200 -n prod`

ops-bot: Running deployment change for deployment/configfetch. Patch applied to replicas=5, env updated. Rolling update started.

Sam (eng-runtime): scaling DB pool on configfetch pods: `kubectl exec -it deploy/configfetch -- /bin/sh -c "export DB_MAX_CONNS=80 && supervisorctl restart configfetch"` — triggered.

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Rollout status: configfetch rollout completed (5/5 ready). No unhealthy pods reported.

Maya (SRE): monitoring metrics now. Within ~60s after rollout we see p95 drop back toward baseline; p99 improving but still elevated. featureflags 429s reduced ~80%. However, streaming stalls still observed for a small fraction of sessions — likely tail traces still hitting a queued DB wait.

Ira (mlops): deployed client-side fallback to use cached flags when server times out (feature gate `ff_local_cache=true`). Rolling that out to streaming proxies (canary 5%). Will monitor errors.

Sam (eng-runtime): investigating trace bundle trc_8f3b — there are a few sequences where configfetch makes 3 sync calls in startup path sequentially, each blocked on auth-db queries. We should decouple that path. For immediate safety I'll patch to parallelize and stop blocking streaming token negotiation on those calls. Pushing hotfix to PR now.

Maya (SRE): customer impact summary for CS: about 3.1% of streaming sessions experienced stalls >5s during the peak (~01:45-01:55Z). A small set of customers reported reconnects and partial outputs; no data loss reported. Escalating to Customer Success to notify top affected customers (Zoe).

Sam (eng-runtime): hotfix merged and rolled to canary (2 pods). Command: `kubectl rollout status deploy/runtime --namespace prod` — canary stable. I'll roll to 30% if metrics look good.

ops-bot: Deploybot: runtime canary passed healthchecks; promoting to 30%.

Maya (SRE): handoff plan — I'm going offline for a break. Sam, please take the next shift. Action list for oncall after handoff:
- keep `FEATUREFLAGS_CACHE_TTL=300` for 2h, then reduce after postmortem decision
- monitor `inference.streaming_latency_p99` and `controlplane.config_fetch_latency_p95` for regressions
- follow up with infra to size DB pool properly and investigate long-running queries
- track client-side fallback rollout and any regressions (Ira)
- draft incident summary and notify CS for impacted customers

Sam (eng-runtime): taking handoff. I'll keep monitoring until 03:00Z. Next steps I'm executing now: create follow-up ticket INC-2026-391, add retrospective notes, and schedule postmortem. Also will add temporary alert for `featureflags.requests_429_1m > 10` to catch early recurrence.

Maya (SRE): thank you :thumbsup: — documented the timeline and actions in the incident ticket. Leaving notes: root cause (initial): synchronous featureflag fetch in streaming init + control-plane DB pool exhaustion + burst in 429s leading to cascading retries and increased tail latency. Mitigations applied: local TTL, circuit-breaker, pool scale, client fallback, and runtime hotfix.

Ira (mlops): confirm we will follow up to change FF SDK to have default local caching and non-blocking startup checks.

Lin (infra): filing infra task to audit DB connection usage and add visibility for long-running configfetch queries. Will propose connection pooling improvements and slow query logging.

ops-bot: Incident updated: INC-2026-391 created, severity: Sev2, status: mitigated.

Sam (eng-runtime): handing official ownership (oncall) note: will run a 1h watch and then hand back at 03:00Z or earlier if stable. I'll post a short postmortem template tomorrow with action owners.

Maya (SRE): thanks team — nice quick coord. Leaving channel. :wave:
